thread:
mia: Heads-up — after the kernel roll (v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0) I'm seeing intermittent tail latency spikes on dedicated clusters for tool/function-calling workloads. 3-10% p95/p99 regressions, reproducible on two machines in eu-west. Opening a thread to gather traces/profiles.

raj: Which exact workload mix? toolcall-heavy vs long free-text generation with structured JSON?

mia: Toolcall-heavy + structured outputs (lots of stop-token boundaries and function-call pauses). My hypothesis: the new kernel selection heuristic is picking a kernel that's worse for short-sequence, pause-heavy flows, and batching heuristics shrink batches when we hit tool pauses. Also KV-cache hit rate dips during pauses -> extra recompute. Attaching a small sampled profile from a live host: 

mia: ```
PROFILE SAMPLE (live-sample):
- time window: 2026-03-16T11:12:03Z
- decode_loop_avg: 19.2ms -> 21.6ms (+12%)
- p95 queue_wait_ms: 18ms -> 35ms
- kernel chosen distribution: matmul_opt_v2 50%, matmul_fused_v1 30%, fallback_generic 20%
- avg_batch_tokens: 64 -> 45 (during spike windows)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 87% -> 74% (when tool pauses accumulate)
- tool_pause_events: 1.2k/min
```

olivia: Do you have a trace with the actual pause points? we need to know if the pause triggers a KV eviction or a cache pointer reset. That would explain re-compilation/reload cost.

mia: I do — minimal trace snippet: 

mia: ```
TRACE (excerpt):
[DECODE] step 34: emit token "\u003cfunc_call\u003e" -> enter TOOL_PAUSE_WAIT_FOR_FN
[KV] preserve=false -> free_temp_segment(0x7f...)
[QUEUE] batch flush triggered (size 18 tokens)
[DECODE] resume: kernel re-eval -> selected matmul_opt_v2, compile_path=hot
```

sam: That free_temp_segment on pause is worrying. Why preserve=false? We usually preserve KV across synchronous toolcalls where the runtime just pauses and resumes — we may be over-eager in safety logic.

raj: Another angle: new kernel (matmul_opt_v2) has better throughput for long streams but slightly worse per-invocation overhead. If batching heuristics see smaller batches (because tool pauses and token_budget targets are conservative), overhead dominates. Do we have continuous batching config?

mia: Current config on the affected pool: 

mia: ```
continuous_batching:
  max_batch_wait_ms: 12
  token_budget_per_request: 256
  batch_token_target: 1024
  max_concurrent_batches: 8
  prefer_low_latency: true
```

raj: prefer_low_latency flag will bias toward earlier dispatch (smaller batches). For toolcall-heavy flows we should try relaxing it or increasing batch_token_target so we amortize kernel overhead. Also try increasing max_batch_wait_ms to 20ms as an experiment.

olivia: On the KV side: we have a safety path that sets preserve=false if structured output contains certain tool markers (to avoid cross-call leakage). Could we change that to a conditional: preserve=true if the toolcall is synchronous and we detect no external state mutation? There's a memory/correctness tradeoff.

mia: I ran a local A/B: keep KV across pause + force kernel to matmul_fused_v1 for short sequences. Result: p95 latency drops from ~240ms -> ~170ms on the reproducer. Cost went up ~5% due to slightly lower throughput but overall unit latency improved.

infra-bot: Deploy helper: Kernel allowlist toggle available: `kernels.allowlist=<model>:matmul_fused_v1` — can be rolled via rollout flag on the pool. Also have quicktoggle for batching params in the pool config.

sam: Good data. Action items: (1) raj to capture perf counters and microbench matmul kernels for short sequence lengths; (2) olivia to propose KV preservation policy change with safety checks; (3) ops to run a canary with increased batch_token_target and pinned kernel on one dedicated pool.

raj: I'll post perf counters and a small reproducer by EOD. I'll include L1/L2 cache miss rates and small-matrix GEMM microbench for N<=64 and N<=128 (short sequence kernels).

mia: Thanks. One more note — watch stop-token handling: some structured-output models emit the tool marker as part of same chunk; our stop-token scanning currently forces a flush which breaks prefix caching. Might need to treat stop-token as soft boundary for caching purposes.

sam: Agreed. We'll prioritize changes that don't violate correctness but improve amortization for short, pause-prone workloads.

mia: :thumbsup: I'll collate traces and add them to the ticket once raj posts counters.
